 • Mireuseom Island - You can enjoy a variety of beautiful flowers on Island. The most popular one is the pandan grass road formed around the Jinjiang River, which is the best place to visit. In addition, if you go in the direction of Gongju Bridge, you will see even more beautiful scenery. 

 • Jeonju Hanok Village - i s comprised of some 700 beautiful hanok buildings, and is Korea's largest, and only urban, traditional hanok village. The village started in the early 1900s around the areas of Gyeonggijeon Shrine, Omokdae, and Jeonjuhyanggyo Confusian Academy - all important cultural heritages.

days_detail.desc:
• Naejangsan National Park - is a famous mountain in Jeonbuk-do, and the best mountain in Korea to view the fall foliage. Because of the bright autumn leaves that blanket Naejangsan Mountain in fall, the mountain is also referred to as Geumgang of Honam, referencing the beautiful Geumgangsan Mountain. 

 • Naejangsa Temple - cradled within the stunning Naejangsan National Park, is believed to have been established in the year 636, within the Baekje Kingdom. Historically, the site once hosted about 50 large temple buildings. However, they were destroyed during foreign invasions of Korea and the Korean War. Most of the structures standing today were reconstructed later. 

 Accommodation: Jeonju Lahan or Jeonju Best Western or Guangju Ramada or Mokpo Hyundai Lahan or similar

days_detail.desc:
• Soswaewon Garden - s a private garden from the Joseon period where Korea's traditional beauty is preserved. Soswaewon Garden presents itself as a clean and transparent garden where the righteous enjoy the life of anbinnakdo (being comfortable amid poverty and taking pleasure in an honest lifestyle) surrounded by a bamboo grove. 

 • Damyang Metasequoia Lined Road - is one of Korea's most beautiful paths. Metasequoia trees were planted along the street in the early 1970s by the Ministry of Internal Affairs after National Road 24 was rebuilt. Thanks to these stately trees, in 2002 the Korea Forest Service selected the boulevard as one of the most beautiful roads in Korea. 

 • Damyang Meta Provence - is a tourist complex located in Damyang, which attracts approximately 5 million tourists a year. Meta Provence consists of fashion streets, design handicraft workshops, commercial spaces, banquet halls and many other open spaces where culture, art and business coexist to provide great experiences for not only individual tourists but also families and groups, and, through diverse and differentiated high-quality services, it strives to provide special memories and new experiences to all visitors.

days_detail.desc:
• Naganeupseong Walled Town - The fortress walls were built using square-shaped stones to reach 4 meters in height, 3 to 4 meters in width, and 1,410 meters in total length. The town consists of three neighborhoods along the east, south and west of the fortress walls. The village is overall well preserved, allowing visitors to observe houses and lifestyles that have all been passed down from the past. The town is highly valued as a historical and cultural resource for studying traditional folk customs. 

 • Suncheonman Wetland - is one of the world's top five coastal wetlands, stretching along a 3km river with mudflats and reed beds. The reed colonies serve as wintering and breeding grounds for various birds such as Hooded Cranes. The tidal flats are home to diverse species including Mudskippers and East Asian Seepweed.

A statue of Kim Gu - a leader, an educator, a politician - symbolizes the spirit of patriotism which led to the Korea's independence.  Includes 1 complimentary Green Tea Ice Cream. 


 • Sumokwon Night Market – A unique forest night market located inside Jeju’s oldest pine tree colony. Opened in 2018, it is Korea’s first nature-based night market, supporting multicultural families and local start-ups within a lively theme-park complex.

days_detail.title: JEJU ISLAND
days_detail.desc:
• 9.81 Theme Park (includes 3 rides) – Korea’s first non-motorized racing theme park, where you can experience eco-friendly gravity racing. Enjoy thrilling downhill runs powered by gravity (9.81 m/s²) with views of the Jeju sea, and relaxed uphill rides facing Hallasan. 


 • Yongmeori Beach – A dramatic hydrovolcanic rocky shoreline formed by underwater eruptions. Its layered cliffs resemble a dragon’s head (“Yongmeori”) and create stunning coastal scenery. Walk along the seaside trail and see the Hamel Monument, marking the spot where Hendrick Hamel drifted ashore. 


 • The Cliff Café – A stylish beachside café with sunbeds and parasols set across a large open space, offering a Southeast Asian-inspired atmosphere. Drink excluded. 


 • Jeju Tangerine Sangria + Stamp Making – Create Jeju-style tangerine sangria using local fruits, then craft a personalized stamp from native Jeju wood as a memorable keepsake. 


 Accommodation: Gloucester Hotel Jeju or similar.

days_detail.title: JEJU ISLAND
days_detail.desc:
• Mt. Hallasan Trekking (Eoseungsaengak Course, approx. 1.5 hours) – Trek Korea’s tallest peak at 1,950m, one of the nation’s three spirit mountains. This scenic trail showcases rich vegetation and diverse wildlife, highlighting Hallasan’s remarkable ecological value. 


 • Jeju Local Tea Omakase – Enjoy a curated tasting of 4 local teas paired with 6 traditional tea confectioneries. 


 • Hueree Natural Park – A nature park at the foot of Hallasan where you can stroll along Jeju Olle trails and enjoy charming black pig performances. 


 • Foot Bath Experience – Soothe your feet with a relaxing herbal foot bath using medicinal herbal packs. 


 Accommodation: Gloucester Hotel Jeju or similar.

 • Snoopy Garden – Meet Snoopy and the Peanuts characters in themed halls designed around “Peanuts, Nature & Life.” Explore five themed spaces and browse the Peanuts Store at Snoopy Garden House.

 Daejeon .

 that offer a serene and rejuvenating experience in a natural setting. 

 • Daejeon Shinsegae Art & Science - is a culture and art complex containing cultural and art contents and the identity of Daejeon as the science capital of Korea. It was designed by a consortium of the Shinsegae Group and Kyeryong Construction Industrial and was built with five underground floors and 43 ground floors over a section of the Expo Science Park site. 

 • Expo Aquarium - a departure from traditional aquariums, as it integrates media art installations, providing an abundance of photo-worthy spots and interactive experiences, such as fish feeding opportunities. 

 • Expo Science Park - That boasts iconic landmarks such as Expo Bridge, Hanbit Tower, Expo Memorial Hall, World Expo Memorial Museum, and Daejeon Traffic Culture Institute.

• Cheongnamdae (former Presidential Villa) - Which means "Cheong Wa Dae in a warm southern land," was once a private villa used by former presidents of Korea. The total area spans 1,825,000 ｍ² and consists of a main building, golf range, heliport, and fishing area. The natural environment surrounding the area has been well preserved, serving as a home to wildlife, including over 143 species of wild flowers and 124 species of trees as well as several endangered species. 

 • Gyejoksan Red Clay Trail (barefoot walking) - Offers a tranquil and soothing opportunity to 

 walk barefoot through the beautiful natural landscapes of Gyejoksan Mountain. Red clay is renowned for its numerous health advantages, as it is rich in essential minerals like potassium, iron, and calcium. Furthermore, it serves as a natural purifier, antioxidant, disinfectant, and detoxifier. This clay emits infrared rays that the body absorbs, aiding in improved blood circulation and cell regeneration. 

 • PHIL Hospital - Where traditional Korean Chuna therapy, a traditional manual therapy that focuses on spinal adjustments and joint mobilization to promote overall health and wellness 

 and Facial Acupuncture therapy, a treatment that boosts lymphatic and circulatory systems, nourishing and oxygenating skin cells, while internally promoting collagen and elastin production that contributes to both a rejuvenated appearance and improved overall skin health. 

 • Hyundai Premium Outlet - A high-end shopping

• Daecheongho Lake Trail - is a 220 kilometer walking path passing through the Daejeon (Dong-gu, Daedeok-gu) and Chungcheongbuk-do (Cheongwon, Okcheon, Boeun) areas. The road passes Daecheongho Lake, small streams, trekking roads, a forest trail, an old path, and much more. 

 • Haru Scalp - a holistic clinic devoted to scalp wellness, where tailored scalp assessments, soothing therapeutic massages with treatments, and a serene atmosphere come together to ensure absolute relaxation and revitalization. 

 • Euneujeongi Culture Street - Is a street located in Daejeon's original city center, resembling Seoul's Myeongdong area. It features clothing stores, restaurants, cafés, and even the flagship store of Daejeon's iconic bakery, "Sung Sim Dang." Close to Daejeon Station, it hosts the annual "Zero 0' Clock Festival," inspired by the tradition of trains departing from Daejeon Station at midnight in the past. 

 • So-dong Café Street - Is a charming district, known for its picturesque streets, cozy cafes, and vibrant atmosphere.

days_detail.desc:
Start your day early with a breathtaking, hour long hot air balloon ride (if weather conditions are unfavorable or if necessary, the experience will be rescheduled to the following morning) and witness the mesmerizing sunrise with panoramic views from above. 

 • Baekje Cultural Land - is the largest history-themed park in Korea, built to share the beautiful culture of the Baekje Kingdom with the world. The large site is filled with traces of Baekje culture. Sabigung Palace is a reconstruction of a real royal palace from the Three Kingdoms period. 

 • Baekmagang River Hwangpo Sailboat - Quietly floats on the Imjingang River moving with the wind with its broad and yellow sail stretched out. Hop on a Hwangpo sailboat, which was a major means of transportation in the Joseon Dynasty and enjoy the beauty of the red cliffs of Imjingang for about 45 minutes from Duji-ri to Jajang-ri. 

 • Nakhwaam Rock - Is a rock cliff towering over Baengmagang River in the northern end of Busosan Mountain. According to the legend, this is where the royal court women of Baekje jumped off to kill themselves when the kingdom of Baekje was defeated during the invasion of Sabiseong Fortress (now Busosanseong Fortress in Buyeo) by the Shilla-Tang Alliance. 

 • Gungnamji Pond - A Historic Site located in Seodong Park, is Korea’s first artificial pond and was created by King Mu from the Baekje dynasty, who fell in love with and eventually married Princess Seonhwa. Gungnamji, literally means a pond i

 • Dongdaemun Market - Is one of Korea’s most well-known markets. It was founded in December 1970 as the largest of its kind in Asia and has maintained that status for the last 40 years. The tower contains galleries, cafés, and a luxury hotel, in addition to a skywalk and an observation deck. It is one of the best spots to appreciate the breathtaking view of Seoul's vibrant city lights. 

 • Goto Mall (Under Ground Shopping Mall) - Gangnam Terminal Underground Shopping Center is often referred to as "Goto Mall" in short. Over 600 stores are lined up on both sides of the two long, parallel corridors featuring clothing, fashion accessories, interior products, and flowers.

 • Myeongdong - I s one of the primary shopping districts in Seoul.

It has been a destination for healthy living, offering both farming experiences and wellness activities. Another popular experience is the "Herbal Foot Bath," where you can enjoy a soothing foot soak with a blend of six herbs grown at the farm. This 20-30 minute session includes meditation, stretching, and a guided video to enhance your relaxation. 

 *Will replaced to Jinhae Cherry Blossom Festival from 25 Mar - 03 Apr

 • Sacheon Namildae Beach (Elephant Shape Rock) - home to the huge Elephant Rock that resembles an elephant drinking water, Namildae Beach is a popular vacation spot all year round thanks to its clean water and soft sand. The thick surrounding forests and Jinneol Observation Deck, as well as many fishing spots, add to its popularity. 

 *Will replaced to Jinhae Cherry Blossom Festival from 25 Mar - 03 Apr 



 • Nine View Café (Stairway to Heaven) - features a striking white staircase sculpture called "Stairway to Heaven" outside, offering the perfect backdrop for capturing emotional and beautiful photos. The terrace on the first floor of the mai

days_detail.title: NAMHAE
days_detail.desc:
• Namhae Geumsan Boriam Hermitage (30m walk to Hermitage) - S its atop Geumsan Mountain (alt. 704 m) . The mountain was once called Bogwangsan Mountain as it was home to Bogwangsa Temple, founded by Monk Wonhyo. 

 • Daraengi Village - is famous for terraced rice paddies on a steep hill on the outskirts of Seolheulsan Mountain. The picturesque rice paddies make up 108 steps (consisting of stones and soil) and are great for taking photographs. 

 • Naengcheon Fishing Village (inc. digging clams) - is a coastal village with a rich history, particularly its connection to the Imjin War. During this conflict, the naval forces under General Yi Sun-sin were stationed here, and it is said that they often drank water from a spring in the village. 

 • Namhae Treasure Island Observatory - is a structure that embodies a "lighthouse that beautifully lights up Namhae," the southernmost tip of Korea. The 360° panoramic view from inside the building is equivalent to what can be seen from an ultra-luxury cruise ship and is difficult to find anywhere else in the country. *included drinks 



 Accommodation: Pension Style

days_detail.title: NAMHAE - HADONG
days_detail.desc:
• Sangsang Sheep Ranch (inc. feeding sheep & bird) - Surrounded by a vast 100,000-pyeong pasture and a cypress forest, the farm offers a peaceful and natural retreat. The cypress trees, along with other surrounding foliage, release phytoncides - natural antimicrobial substances known for their health benefits. Phytoncides are most abundant in coniferous trees like cypress, and they are believed to help clear the mind, alleviate skin conditions, and promote relaxation. Visitors can enjoy a leisurely walk around the farm while breathing in the fresh, healing air. 

 • Hadong Samseonggung - is a Taoist shrine located at 850 meters above sea level on Jirisan Mountain. It serves as a spiritual hub for practicing Sinseondo, embodying traditional Korean culture. 

 • Hadong Tea Museum (Inc: DIY Dasik Making and try with Tea) - It aims to promote the tea culture of the area, the first tea producer in the nation, while advertising the quality and superiority of Hadong green tea. 

 • Hadong Hwagae Market - is one of the five biggest traditional market, which once flooded with people. A market that offers a variety of local products and delicacies, you could count the number of markets of this scale in Korea on one hand. 



 Accommodation: Kensington Hotel & Resort Hadong or similar property

Good medicinal herbs were also found in Jirisan Mountain. Sancheong is also well known as the place where Heo Jun practiced medicine. 

 • Suseonsa Temple - is a temple situated on Ungseokbong Peak in Jirisan Mountain. Renowned for its picturesque hydrangea and lotus, it has become a favored destination for many visitors. 

 • Hapcheon Film Park - is filled with a unique atmosphere and things to see in every alley, and has been used as a filming location for over 190 dramas, movies, and music videos set in the 1920s to the 1980s. Visitors can look around using trams, wagons, and more while they take pictures of every place. 

 After that, transfer back to Busan.

• Daewangam Suspension Bridge - is the first suspension bridge in Ulsan and the first large-scale commercial tourism facility in Dong-gu. It was created with a length of 303 meters, connecting Hatgaebi and Surubang coastal trails in Daewangam Park. 

 • Taehwagang Bamboo Forest - is a bamboo forest that stretches over about 4 km along the Taehwagang River and is a natural garden using bamboo that has grown naturally for a long time. It is a healing space in the city where the river wind blowing through the bamboo and the whisper of bamboo leaves tickle your ears. 

 • Ulsan Onggi Museum - was established when earthenware master Heo Deok-man settled in the area in 1975. The village today showcases a massive collection of various earthenware products, which creates a unique sight. Over 50% of the country's earthenware products are crafted at this village. 

 • Busan Jagalchi Cruise (Night View) - is a 3 story ship that weighs 379 tons and can board over 300 passengers. Departing from the dockyard which is located in Jagalchi Market, explores the pleasant scenery as well as the sea with full of life 



 Accommodation: Avani Central Hotel or similar property

• Taejongdae Cliffed Coast (inc. Danubi Train) - Is one of the most famous tourist sites in Busan. Because of how old and famous the park is, it tends to fly under the radar for many tourists who are familiar with Busan. 

 • Arte Museum - is a global immersive media art exhibition that creates new exhibits in each region under the theme of ‘Eternal Nature’, spreading both domestically and internationally. It is known for showcasing works that incorporate the nature and cultural heritage of each region. Arte Museum Busan is particularly unique, with 16 out of 19 media art pieces newly created specifically for Busan. 

 • Oryukdo Sky Walk - meaning a saddle, due to the shape of the point. It was also called Jallokgae by residents and female divers in the area. isitors will be thrilled with the view of the waves while looking down through the transparent floor. The sea stretches out ahead of the skywalk, perfect for a photo op. 

 • Jagalchi Market - I s Korea's largest seafood market, selling both live and dried fish. This market represents Busan and is famous throughout the country. Visitors can eat fresh raw fish right at the market. 

 • BIFF Square - Having been remade into a cultural tourist attraction promoting the advancement of Korea’s film industry, BIFF Square has contributed to Busan’s newfound status as an international cultural tourist city. 



 Accommodation: Avani Central Hotel or similar property

 natural ingredients like herbs and antioxidants, supporting detoxification and overall liver function.

days_detail.title: SEOUL TO JEJU ISLAND - A DAY OF DISCOVERIES
days_detail.desc:
At the start of your day, a charter will whisk you away from your hotel to Gimpo International Airport, where a domestic flight awaits to fly you into the captivating world of Jeju Island. Here, you'll delve into the essence of Jeju's culture and beauty. Your exploration will encompass the awe-inspiring Yongduam Rock, the mystic Mysterious Road, the treasure trove of tradition at Jeju Folklore and Natural History Museum, and the bustling Dongmun Traditional Market. 



 Accommodation: Best Western Hotel or similar property

attractions_detail.name_cn: 雪绿茶博物馆·悦诗风吟

days_detail.hotel: Best Western Hotel or similar property
days_detail.title: UNVEILING JEJU’S NATURAL WONDERS
days_detail.desc:
This day is dedicated to exploring the natural wonders of Jeju Island. You'll ascend to the summit of the UNESCO World Natural Heritage site known as "Sunrise Peak" at Seongsan Ilchulbong," where the panoramic view is a reward in itself. Following this, your journey continues with a visit to Seongeup Folk Village, a living testament to traditional Korean culture. The day is sprinkled with the joy of fruits picking (based on the fruits in season) at fruits orchard. You'll also have the opportunity to explore the fascinating columnar jointing formations at the Osulloc Tea Museum and finally experience the mesmerizing Cheonjiyeon Falls. 



 Accommodation: Best Western Hotel or similar property

days_detail.hotel: Asti Hotel or Crown Harbor or similar property
days_detail.title: JEJU ISLAND TO BUSAN - A JOURNEY OF CONTRASTS
days_detail.desc:
A seamless transition takes you from Jeju Island to Busan as you board a domestic flight departing from Jeju International Airport and arriving at Gimhae International Airport. Busan, South Korea's second-largest city, promises a day of stark contrasts and captivating experiences. Your adventure includes a visit to the enchanting Gamcheon Cultural Village, known for its colorful houses and artistic charm. The Songdo Sky Walk provides breathtaking panoramic views of the cityscape. After lunch, dive into the vibrant energy of Nampo-dong (including BIFF Street, etc.) , often referred to as Busan's Myeongdong. Don't miss the chance to savor local delicacies at the popular Jagalchi Fish Market and explore the eclectic offerings of Gukje Market.

days_detail.title: BUSAN’S COASTAL CHARMS
days_detail.desc:
The day begins with an enchanting exploration of Haeundae Blueline Park, your adventure continues with a ride on the Blueline Train to admire the natural beauty and tranquility of Haeundae beach. Next, explore Busan X The Sky, an awe-inspiring observation deck, offering unrivaled panoramic views of the cityscape and beyond. It's a must-visit spot for breathtaking vistas. Embark on a spiritual visit to Haedong Yonggungsa Temple perched on a cliff overlooking the sea. Stroll through the lively Haeundae Traditional Market, where the hustle and bustle of local life come alive with a rich array of vendors, street food, and traditional treasures waiting to be discovered. Bask in the modernity of The Bay 101, a chic waterfront complex with a yacht club, trendy shops & open-air bars & restaurants. Spend time shopping at Shinsegae Centum City, the largest department store recorded in the Guinness World Records. 



 Accommodation: Asti Hotel or Crown Harbor or similar property

days_detail.hotel: Amanty Hotel or Seoul Garden or Seoul Dragon City or similar property
days_detail.title: BUSAN TO SEOUL - A RETURN TO THE CAPITAL
days_detail.desc:
Bid farewell to Busan as you embark on a domestic flight from Gimhae International Airport to Seoul's Gimpo International Airport. Back in the capital, Seoul awaits with its blend of modernity and tradition. 

 Your day unfolds with visits to unique destinations like RealWorld, an immersive mission-based gaming experience platform cum café (1x drink included per pax) in the charming Seongsu-dong, then explore the innovative shopping space of Common Ground, and the intriguing Space Wadiz, an offline platform for a hands-on experience with crowdfunding products. Visit Myeongdong, Seoul's bustling district, combines shopping, dining, and culture. By day, it's a shopper's paradise; by night, it's alive with street food and entertainment, offering a complete urban experience. 



 Accommodation: Amanty Hotel or Seoul Garden or Seoul Dragon City or similar property

days_detail.hotel: Amanty Hotel or Seoul Garden or Seoul Dragon City or similar property
days_detail.title: A JOURNEY THROUGH SEOUL’S HISTORIC AND CULTURAL TREASURES
days_detail.desc:
Delve into Seoul’s rich history and culture with visits to iconic landmarks such as Gyeongbokgung Palace, a historic filming hotspot, and the Blue House, the former presidential residence. Explore the world of authentic Korean ginseng, discovering traditional remedies and wellness products crafted from this revered root. Experience Korea’s innovative beauty scene at a skincare and cosmetics showroom, showcasing natural ingredients, effective products, and unique packaging. Wander through Ikseon-dong, a historic neighborhood of hanoks converted into cafes, shops, and cultural spaces, then conclude at Gwangjang Market, one of Seoul’s oldest markets, famous for its street food and textiles, offering a true taste of local life.



 Accommodation: Amanty Hotel or Seoul Garden or Seoul Dragon City or similar property

days_detail.title: SEOUL - INCHEON - SINGAPORE
days_detail.desc: Your South Korean adventure culminates with a day of immersive cultural experiences. Explore Korean wellness centre that promotes liver health with natural ingredients like herbs and antioxidants, supporting detoxification and overall liver function. Engage in Korean culinary creativity with a hands-on food DIY experience . Craft and savor the beloved Gimbap as featured in "The Extraordinary Attorney Woo". Embrace the elegance of traditional Hanbok attire and capture unforgettable moments on cameras. The grand finale of your journey unfolds at Starfield Shopping Mall in Goyang, a world-class shopping destination. It is time to bid farewell to South Korea and travel home with fond memories of the sights, sounds and stories we have collected on this incredible journey. We hope that you have had an enjoyable holiday with Dynasty Travel and look forward to our next trip together!

days_detail.title: SEOUL - GIMPO - JEJU ISLAND
days_detail.desc:
Board a domestic flight to Jeju Island and begin with Yongduam Rock, or Dragon Head Rock, a natural formation shaped like a dragon’s head. Explore ARTE Museum, Korea’s largest interactive multimedia art exhibition, featuring immersive galleries inspired by tropical rainforests, swamps, and outer space, engaging sight, sound, and scent for a truly sensory experience. Finish the day at Dongmun Traditional Market, Jeju’s oldest and largest market, offering a vibrant mix of local delicacies, fresh seafood, and unique merchandise.



Accommodation: Grand Hyatt or similar property

days_detail.hotel: Grand Hyatt or similar property
days_detail.title: JEJU ISLAND
days_detail.desc:
Seongsan Ilchulbong (Sunrise Peak), a 5,000-year-old UNESCO volcanic crater, offers some of Jeju’s most beautiful sunrise views. The island’s rich farmland also makes it perfect for seasonal fruit picking directly from local orchards. For a taste of Jeju’s creativity, enjoy a unique pizza-making workshop featuring island ingredients like Jeju pork ham and beet butter. The journey concludes at Jeongbang Waterfall—the only waterfall in Korea that drops straight into the sea—set against scenic coastal trails and dramatic ocean views.



 Accommodation: Grand Hyatt or similar property

days_detail.title: JEJU ISLAND - BUSAN
days_detail.desc:
Board a domestic flight to Busan and explore its scenic and cultural highlights. Visit Taejongdae, a coastal park with stunning cliffs and greenery, best enjoyed on the Danubi Train for a leisurely tour of its picturesque spots. Wander through Gamcheon Cultural Village, the “Machu Picchu of Busan,” with vibrant murals, sculptures, and winding streets. Discover the bustling Nampo-dong district, home to street markets, dining options, and landmarks like Jagalchi Fish Market, BIFF Square, and Yongdusan Park. Explore Bupyeong Kkangtong Market for unique secondhand and vintage finds, then end the day at Jagalchi Market, where fresh seafood can be purchased and prepared on the spot.



Accommodation: Lotte Hotel or similar property

Visit Beomeosa Temple, a historic 7th-century Buddhist site renowned for its stunning architecture, serene mountain setting, and cultural significance. Stroll along Haeundae Blueline Park, a coastal trail with scenic beach and ocean views, best enjoyed on a leisurely train ride through the landscape. Relax at The Spaland, a luxurious jjimjilbang (Korean sauna and spa) inside Shinsegae Centum City, the world’s largest department store. End the day exploring Ppangcheon-dong, a vibrant neighborhood famous for its street food, offering a variety of breads, pastries, and local snacks from lively vendors and small shops.

days_detail.desc:
Board a domestic flight to Gimpo Airport to return to Seoul and explore the city’s vibrant highlights. Begin in Insa-dong, a neighborhood rich in traditional culture and arts, where you can create personalized stamps through a seal stone engraving experience. Visit N Seoul Tower atop Namsan Mountain for panoramic views of the city from the iconic 236.7-meter landmark. Conclude the day in Myeongdong, a bustling shopping district filled with trendy boutiques, cosmetics shops, and street food vendors, perfect for fashion, snacks, and the lively urban atmosphere.

days_detail.desc:
Visit Gyeongbokgung Palace, the largest Joseon Dynasty royal palace and an iconic site often featured in historic Korean films. Enjoy lunch at a serene restaurant nestled in Seoul’s picturesque hills, offering traditional architecture, garden views, and a cultural dining experience. Stroll through Ikseon-dong, a charming neighborhood of narrow alleys and hanoks converted into modern cafes, shops, and restaurants, and savor a relaxing afternoon tea at a hanok-style café. End the day in Hongdae, a vibrant district known for its indie music, underground culture, clubs, and lively entertainment scene.
